### J-1 A damaged onboarding.json stops every pack, but the docs must never block the stage
- quote: "SHALL NOT block the stage"
- situation (adversary): `.nio/project/onboarding.json` is half-written or hand-edited. `progress` raises `ValueError(".nio/project/onboarding.json is not valid: fix or restore it")`. `docs_for` doesn't catch it, and neither do `pack.build` (reader branch), `jury._pack_text` or `implement.worker_pack`. Every worker pack and every scope or architecture-fit juror pack then fails or crashes. A docs file that only helps a reader ends up blocking the spec, plan and implement stages. If a caller swallows the error instead, the pack ships with no docs and no line saying why.
- fix: in `docs_for`, catch the `ValueError` and emit a `onboarding: unreadable: fix .nio/project/onboarding.json` line, or let the stage commands print the error and stop. Pick one and test it.
- validation: confirmed: `onboard.progress` (onboard.py:65-77) raises ValueError on a bad onboarding.json, and `docs_for` (onboard.py:186) and `_pairs` call it with no catch, so pack.py:82 and jury.py:1362 fail for every reader. Nothing in the artefact says a damaged state file is allowed to stop a pack.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-53

### J-2 A symlinked project doc is read and sent to the model
- quote: "a symlink is never listed or followed"
- situation (adversary): `.nio/project/stack.md` is a symlink, for example to a secrets file or to `~/.ssh/config`, and a cloned repo can carry one. `docs_for` checks `p.is_file()`, which follows links, then runs `p.read_text()`. The target's whole text goes into every worker, plan and architecture-fit pack, and so to the model. `jury.sources` rejects paths outside the repo, but `docs_for` and `worker_pack` have no such check. The scan's own rule says it never follows a symlink.
- fix: in `docs_for`, skip any doc that is a symlink or whose resolved path is outside the root, and add a `missing:` line for it.
- validation: confirmed: `docs_for` (onboard.py:188-193) uses `p.is_file()` and `p.read_text()`, which follow symlinks, and has no root check. The `resolve().is_relative_to` check exists only in `jury.sources` (jury.py:218). The worker and plan packs read the link target unchecked.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-54

### J-3 The apps line is read from anywhere in the spec, in one form only, and a wrong read drops docs silently
- quote: "the apps are those the slug's spec names in `apps`"
- situation (adversary): `_pairs` runs `re.search(r"^apps:\s*\[?([^\n\]]*)", spec.read_text(), re.M)` on the whole file. A line starting `apps:` in the body wins over a missing front-matter key. The spec drafter or a quoted intake can write one, for example `apps: web` in an example block. Then only `web/` docs are mapped, and the `api` stack and architecture never reach the plan or worker pack. Nothing is named missing, because unmapped docs aren't listed. The block form `apps:\n  - api` gives `[""]`, matches no app, and falls back to all apps. So the narrowing is silently lost and the pack is bigger than the table says. A name in `apps:` that matches no onboarded app, such as a typo, also falls back to all apps without a word.
- fix: parse only the front matter (the first `---` block) and accept both list forms. When the spec names an app that isn't onboarded, add a line saying so.
- validation: confirmed: `_pairs` (onboard.py:172) runs `^apps:` with re.M over the whole spec, not just the front matter. The block form is read as the text `- api`, which matches no app, and `or apps` falls back to all apps without a word. Both the typo case and the block-form case narrow nothing and say nothing.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-55

### J-4 worker_pack splits the pack on a text match, so a memory record can corrupt its structure
- quote: "so the docs sit inside its first part and the pack keeps exactly five `## ` parts"
- situation (adversary): `memory.partition("## Project docs\n")` matches the first occurrence anywhere in the memory pack. A full record whose text contains that heading line, for example a record describing this very feature, is cut there. The rest of the record is then treated as the project docs and the real docs sit below it. Docs stay un-nested but sit under the wrong `###` heading, and the test only checks docs from a clean fixture.
- fix: have `pack.build` return the docs part separately, or look for the marker only after the last record.

### J-5 AC-32 is proved only by a model-run test that the suite skips
- quote: "Without NIO_E2E they print `skipped` and pass."
- situation (conformance): test_ac32_actor_names_persona is the only test for AC-32 (level: e2e). The pack gives its result as "unknown", and the suite that passed runs without NIO_E2E. A pass of that suite therefore says nothing about the persona behaviour of the drafter card or the spec skill, so no run evidence exists for AC-32.
- situation (conformance): the only test for AC-32 is `test_ac32_actor_names_persona`, which prints `skipped` and passes unless NIO_E2E=1 is set. The suite command in the pack sets no such variable. Its `passed` result is reused from T-9 and has no per-test result, so a skipped e2e run and a real pass look the same. The pack therefore holds no evidence that the drafter card produces `P-n` or `no persona` on the actor lines.
- situation (conformance): AC-32 (Level: e2e) is covered only by `test_ac32_actor_names_persona`. That test is gated by `NIO_E2E`, and the suite command sets no such variable. The test therefore printed `skipped` and passed without drafting a spec, so nothing shows that the drafter names P-1 or "no persona". The result in the pack is `unknown`.
- fix: run the e2e test with NIO_E2E=1 and put its pass in the evidence, or have the CLI run it as a TC. Until then AC-32 has no passing test.
- validation: confirmed: tests/test_onboard_e2e.py:3-4 says the test prints `skipped` and passes without NIO_E2E, and `test_ac32_actor_names_persona` is the only test serving AC-32 (tasks.md T-9). A normal suite pass therefore gives no evidence for AC-32.
- disposition: accepted-risk by human: AC-32's e2e test passed at T-9's green with NIO_E2E=1 (run R-261108-7dt6); jury evidence runs without NIO_E2E. Approved by the human 2026-11-14.

### J-6 Packs carry no stale line, though CT-9 and the accepted change require one
- quote: "stale: <doc> (<path> <changed|deleted>)"
- quote: "ponytail: no stale line yet, it needs the docs' source records (CT-7)."
- quote: "nio pack also reads the project docs and hashes their recorded source files"
- situation (consistency): an onboarded project's `stack.md` records a source file that has since changed. A worker or plan pack is built with `docs_for`, which emits no `stale:` line and hashes nothing, so the reader is handed the out-of-date doc with no warning. CT-9 requires that line, and C-261108-mk6n accepts hashing the recorded sources in `nio pack`.
- fix: add the `stale:` line from the CT-7 check to `docs_for`, or record in the spec that stale lines wait for CT-7 in a later effort and that C-261108-mk6n is only partly built.
- validation: refuted: tasks.md schedules stale flags in packs for E-6 (T-22 serves AC-31 with TC-36 and TC-51, after T-21), and `docs_for` states the deferral in its ponytail note. The stale source records and the `stale` function do not exist yet (no `def stale` in onboard.py), so E-3 cannot emit the line.

### J-7 The spec skill passes `--slug` before the spec exists, against CT-16
- quote: "--reader spec --slug <slug>"
- quote: "(and `--slug` once the spec exists)"
- situation (consistency): at step 4 of the spec skill, no `spec.md` exists yet, so `--slug` finds nothing and the pack gets every app. That matches the result without a slug, so no pack is wrong today. But the skill and CT-16 disagree on when `--slug` is passed, and a re-run after `apps:` is written would name the apps a different way than the contract describes.
- fix: pass `--slug` at step 4 only when the spec exists, as CT-16 says, or change CT-16 to match the skill.

### J-8 Quotes from project docs never ground
- quote: "so they are listed under "Files to read" and a quote from them grounds"
- situation (correctness): the architecture-fit lens at the plan gate quotes `.nio/project/principles.md`, which its pack lists. `grounding()` calls `sources(root, slug, gate)` without the lens, so the docs are missing from the ground text and the quote is dropped as ungrounded.
- fix: give `grounding` and its caller the lens, or have `grounding` take the lens's sources. Add a test that runs `grounded` on a quote from a project doc.
- validation: confirmed: `grounding(root, slug, gate)` (jury.py:221-223) calls `sources` with no lens, so `reader` stays None (jury.py:214) and no project docs are added. jury.py:620 passes that text as the ground for `add`/`grounded` (jury.py:811), so a quote from principles.md or personas.md is dropped as ungrounded.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-57
